Product Updates

What we shipped

Technology  •  August 28, 2026

The Discover UI/UX release we've been building toward for months is shipping this Friday and available to clients Monday morning.

Two new clinical conditions, SUD in Remission and Severe Mental Illness, are now tracked across Member Details, filters, and risk scores. Member search now handles hyphenated last names correctly. Report Filters have been renamed and redesigned, opening in a flyout on the right with cleaner labels, better validation, and saved filters rolling over automatically. The Pregnancy and Postpartum landing pages gained row highlighting for easier navigation. Multi-tenant users can now stay logged into multiple organizations simultaneously, and dashboards open in the same tab for faster navigation.

This one has been a long time coming. Nice work to everyone who had a hand in making it happen.

Watch the release walkthrough video →

Analytics  •  August 2026

Last month we introduced the Clinical Intelligence Dashboard, and the response from our provider network has been something else entirely.

The beta version is now live and in the hands of Medical Directors across our affiliate network. Since launch, the team has been actively iterating based on real-world use: Site of Service has been added, Attributed Providers are now visible on the Obstetrics and Gynecology pages, Breast Cancer Screenings now pull from two additional data sources including orders and OBGYN history, and row-level security ensures each Medical Director sees only their market's data.

The providers have noticed. Here's what a few of them had to say:

"After seeing this dashboard in Chicago, I couldn't wait to get back to show my review committee." — Dr. Scanlon, MCW

"I love this high level overview, whereas the other tabs have all of the patient details by provider." — Dr. Courser, Avina Health

"Wrapping into Lucina will be helpful. I may be riding a bike, but she is riding the high powered motorcycle to get into the data and now I'll be able to keep up." — Dr. Suba, UWH TX

That last one says it all. The work this team has put into this dashboard is landing exactly the way it was meant to.

What's Next

Looking ahead

Discover LucinaCare Enablement  •  October 2026

The team is heads down on getting Discover ready for the LucinaCare pilot launch with CareFirst. Four new features are planned to support the pilot.

Engaged Status introduces a new episode status that allows care managers to mark members who have opted into the LucinaCare program, visible in the episode flyout, available as a filter, and supported via bulk action.

Search by Date of Birth expands the existing search experience so care managers can locate members by DOB in addition to Name and Member ID.

A new SMI Condition Flag will surface a visual indicator directly in the conditions grid for members identified with Severe Mental Illness, consistent with how the existing PTB flag is displayed.

The LucinaCare/CareFirst Evaluation Framework will establish the foundation for measuring and reporting on pilot outcomes.

This is the first set of Discover enhancements built specifically around LucinaCare operations, and it sets the team up to support the pilot the right way from day one.

Lindsay's Process Corner

From the process desk

Velocity Tracking

As we continue tracking velocity sprint over sprint, a couple of reminders for the team.

Every ticket that is prioritized and worked on must hit the Dev Done state before moving to QA in order to be counted toward your velocity. If a ticket skips that state transition, it won't be captured, so make sure it moves through Dev Done before it goes anywhere else.

Second, if you have a ticket assigned to you that is missing story points, please add them. Velocity tracking only works when points are in place before the work is complete. If you're unsure how to estimate, refer to the Story Point Estimation Process or bring it to the next planning session.

Get to Know the Team

Aurelia Stout
Senior Director Implementation

Hi, I'm Aurelia! [ah-REEL-ya or ah-REEL-ee-ah, if only I had a buck for every time someone asked]. I grew up in Ohio, lived in Chicago, then headed to Austin in 2013.

I like converting project chaos into successful launches. If I got to pick my own title, I'd go with Cap'n Chaos or Go-Live Whisperer. As an implementation leader, I love helping clients and teams navigate complex projects, translating ambiguity into actionable plans and tackling everything from pesky data issues to tricky timelines. I'm all about solving problems, building scalable processes, bringing people together, and getting a little too excited about a good template.

Outside of work, you'll find me catching a live band, knee-deep in a home improvement project, trying a new restaurant with friends, or hosting a BBQ and pool party. I'm also an avid reader and word game enthusiast, and I love hanging out with my hubby, Dan — my partner-in-crime who joins me for everything from pasta-making and glass-blowing classes to college football games and murder mystery dinners.

Fun Fact: My seven siblings and I have maintained a daily text thread since the 2020 lockdowns where we share our game scores. Competitive much? Word nerds 4-ev-a!

📅 Your calendar for the week just got wiped and rebuilt from scratch. What's the first thing you reschedule?
My own focus block (sorry, future me). At least that's what I'd intend to do. Let's be real — I'd have five client meetings booked before I finished my coffee.
🤝 Your ideal client kickoff call includes:
Ten minutes of small talk, then business. Relationships matter. Agendas matter. The best kickoffs leave room for both.
Michael Lowe
Cloud Lead

I'm Michael, Cloud Lead. I treat our Azure, AWS environments like my own personal Cerebro — monitoring telemetry, automating infrastructure, and keeping the grid secure. I grew up in the orthopedics capital and live in the RV capital. I like CAPITAL LETTERS. I do not own an RV and probably never will (I know how they get made).

When I take off the S.H.I.E.L.D. badge for the day, I'm managing my Docker and Emby server rack, reading fantasy, or planning the next Comic-Con cosplay with my wife and two boys.

A few fun facts:

I own more comic books than you have socks.

I haven't worn deodorant since 2019 (on-site meetups are the sole exception).

I've always had Doctor Strange-level thoughts in my head; thanks to AI, I can finally generate the soundtrack for them.

My tactical doorstep drops to date include: 300 ping pong balls, a giant inflatable swan, and a triple-threat strawberry payload (cheesecake, strawberries, and ice cream).

I'm so mature everyone else looks up to me and wonders how I got this way.
